climate.overview_html: The headline new scientific finding for September 18 is the first statistically confirmed acceleration of global warming: Foster & Rahmstorf, “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly,” Geophysical Research Letters Vol. 53, Issue 17 (September 16, 2026) achieves >98% statistical confidence that the forced warming trend has accelerated since ~2015 across five temperature datasets after removing ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability — faster than any decade in the 177-year record. Prior-window anchors remain current: WMO’s SON 2026 update places Niño 3.4 at ~+3.6°C, peak NDJ forecast +2.4–2.8°C; Super El Niño officially confirmed September 14 (RONI +2.07°C); western Europe’s hottest summer on record at 2.54°C above average, 2,025+ French excess deaths, Rhine at 1880 low; Nepal–Tibet glacier collapse toll ~1,446 dead and ~6,669 missing; NOAA August 2026 warmest August in 177 years (+1.32°C); Copernicus August 2026 joint-hottest month ever (1.65°C above pre-industrial, 16th consecutive month ≥1.5°C).

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast Most Land Areas September–November; Super El Niño at Peak Season
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the confirmed Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026, with significant probability of record-breaking warmth in the tropics and sub-tropics. The update confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27. WMO notes the combined El Niño and positive IOD forcing is the largest co-occurring tropical ocean anomaly since 1997–98.

items.headline: Super El Niño Confirmed: Running ONI Crosses +2.0°C September 14 — First Super El Niño Since 2015–16; Peak Forecast NDJ 2026/27 at +2.4–2.8°C; WMO >95% Probability 2027 Sets Warmest Year Record
items.summary: The Running Oceanic Niño Index crossed the +2.0°C threshold on September 14, 2026, officially qualifying the current event as a Super El Niño — the first since 2015–16, which peaked at +2.6°C. The RONI reached +2.07°C. NOAA and WMO multi-model ensembles forecast a peak of +2.4–2.8°C for November–January 2026/27, with some ensemble members reaching +3.0°C. Continued Atlantic hurricane suppression, drought in eastern Australia and SE Asia, and enhanced precipitation in the Horn of Africa are the primary near-term impacts. WMO assigns >95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record — Western Europe 2.54°C Above 1991–2020 Normal; Rhine at 1880 Historic Low Freight Costs +18–25%; 2,025+ Excess Deaths France; Farm Income Down ~9%; Paks + Cernavodă Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: The Diplomatic Affairs analysis quantifies the cascading economic and humanitarian damage of Europe's record summer 2026 — the hottest in recorded history for western Europe at 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 Copernicus climatology. France recorded its hottest summer ever with 2,025+ excess deaths. The Rhine fell to its lowest navigational level since 1880, pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Low Danube water forced Hungary's Paks-2 nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă plant to curtailed output. French farm income declined approximately 9% from crop failures. The analysis notes these headline tallies exclude longer-term infrastructure damage, ecosystem impacts, health-system strain, and productivity losses — costs 'are only starting to arrive.'

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods ONGOING: ~1,446 Dead; ~6,669 Missing Including 587 Foreign Nationals; $820M+ Pledged; Nepal Climate Emergency Active; UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund Submission Initiated
items.summary: Nepal's NDRRMA confirmed approximately 1,446 total deaths as of September 17, with approximately 6,669 persons missing including 587 foreign nationals from 34 countries. International pledges have reached $820 million. Nepal's parliament's national climate emergency declaration remains active. A formal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission has been initiated — the first to directly implicate European-origin emissions in a documented Himalayan glacier catastrophe. ICIMOD's assessment found the Yanmarang Glacier lost approximately 40% of its volume since 2020. The event remains the deadliest glacier-related disaster in recorded Himalayan history.

items.headline: NOAA NCEI August 2026 Global Climate Report: Warmest August in 177-Year Record at +1.32°C; JJA 2026 Warmest Meteorological Summer Globally; 2026 On Track for Warmest Calendar Year
items.summary: NOAA confirmed August 2026 as the warmest August in 177 years of instrumental records at +1.32°C (+2.38°F) above the 20th-century average, breaking the previous tied record (August 2023 and 2024) by 0.08°C. Meteorological summer (JJA) 2026 was the warmest on record globally at +1.21°C. Northern Hemisphere land temperatures were highest on record for any August. Year-to-date (January–August 2026) global temperatures are the warmest in the 177-year dataset, placing 2026 on trajectory to become the warmest calendar year ever recorded, further elevated by the Super El Niño peak forecast for NDJ 2026/27.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record (Tied July 2023) at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Extra-Polar SSTs All-Time August Record 21.07°C; 16th Consecutive Month ≥1.5°C
items.summary: Copernicus C3S confirms August 2026 as the world's joint-hottest month on record, tied with July 2023 at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline (1850–1900). August 2026 was the 16th consecutive month at or above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. Extra-polar sea surface temperatures set an all-time August record at 21.07°C. 13.2% of global land and ocean surfaces registered record-high temperatures for any August day during the month. The joint-record status means three of the hottest months in recorded history now include two months from 2026.

weather.overview_html: Two records were updated on September 18. First, the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has broken a 60-year record: no hurricane has formed in the entire season as of September 18 — the first time this late in the season has elapsed without a hurricane since 1966, driven by Super El Niño vertical wind shear over the Main Development Region; any hurricane forming from September 19 onward would be the latest first hurricane in the satellite era, and if none forms at all, 2026 would join 1907 and 1914 as the only zero-hurricane Atlantic seasons in 175 years of records. Second, Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan: the system is approaching the Ogasawara Islands with maximum significant wave height of 7.3 m and storm-force winds expected September 18–19; the forecast track curves NNE toward the Kanto/Boso Peninsula and Tokyo area by Monday September 21, directly threatening Silver Week (September 19–23) for an estimated 20 million domestic travelers — Japan’s first five-day consecutive holiday since 2015. Time’s September 17 deep-dive on the SE Asia haze crisis documents 12 million people blanketed and 113,336 respiratory infection cases in Indonesia as of September 9 — worst Indonesian wildfires in 11 years. EFFIS updated Europe’s wildfire total to 668,035 ha on September 16–17 (up from 660,528 ha, nearly double the 20-year average of 346,567 ha).

items.source: JMA / JTWC / Bloomberg / Above The Norm News / Zoom.Earth
items.headline: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan UPDATED September 18: Approaching Ogasawara Islands; 7.3 m Max Wave Height; Storm-Force Winds September 18–19; Kanto/Boso/Tokyo Area September 21; Silver Week Disruption for ~20 Million Domestic Travelers
items.summary: As of 03:00 UTC September 18, Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan is located approximately 324 km east of Iwo To, tracking westward at 28 km/h. The system is approaching the Ogasawara Islands with maximum significant wave height of 7.3 metres and storm-force winds forecast for the island chain September 18–19. After the Ogasawara passage, the system will slow, round the western edge of the subtropical ridge, and accelerate NNE under deep-layer mid-latitude westerlies, with the center forecast approximately 100 km off the Boso Peninsula and 180 km from central Tokyo by Monday September 21. JMA has issued warnings for the Ogasawara chain; mainland Kanto/Izu/Tohoku advisories are expected to follow September 18. The approach coincides with Silver Week (September 19–23), Japan's first five-day consecutive holiday since 2015, placing approximately 20 million domestic travelers at disruption risk. Bloomberg's September 17 report described the system as set to 'drench Tokyo over the long holiday weekend.'

items.source: CBS News / Yahoo News / Houma Times / NOAA NHC
items.headline: Atlantic Hurricane Season Breaks 60-Year Record September 18: No Hurricane Formed in 2026 — First Since 1966 This Late Without a Hurricane; 5 Named Storms Zero Hurricanes ACE 4.4; Season Could Join 1907 and 1914 as Zero-Hurricane Year in 175-Year Record
items.summary: As of September 18, the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has gone without producing a single hurricane — breaking the 60-year record for the latest first Atlantic hurricane, the last occurrence being 1966. The season has produced five named tropical storms (Ana, Bill, Claudette, Danny, Edouard), none of which reached hurricane strength. Accumulated Cyclone Energy stands at 4.4 units, among the lowest on record for this point in the season. Any hurricane forming from September 19 onward would be the latest first hurricane in the satellite era; if no hurricane forms at all in 2026, it would join 1907 and 1914 as the only years in the 175-year historical record with zero Atlantic hurricanes. NOAA's below-normal forecast attributes the suppressed activity to Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear over the Main Development Region, expected to persist through November 30 when hurricane season officially closes.

items.source: Time / Wikipedia / ASMC ASEAN / Mongabay / ABC News Australia
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze UPDATED: Time Magazine September 17 — 12 Million People Blanketed; 113,336 Respiratory Cases in Indonesia (Sept 9, Double Prior Week); Japan CH-47 Chinooks Deployed Kalimantan September 12–19; Worst Indonesian Wildfires in 11 Years; Fires Through October/November
items.summary: Time magazine's September 17 comprehensive report documents the 2026 Southeast Asian haze crisis as the worst Indonesian wildfires in 11 years, with more than 12 million people blanketed in thick smog across Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. As of September 9, Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces — double the figure recorded a week earlier. At least 200,000+ hectares have burned across Borneo and Sumatra. Malaysia declared a state of emergency in parts of Sarawak, closing 647 schools across 12 districts. Singapore recorded unhealthy air quality across every region for the first time since 2019. Japan deployed three CH-47 Chinook helicopters and personnel to West Kalimantan for aerial water-bombing operations September 12–19. Indonesian authorities warn fires could continue through October or early November under the Super El Niño-driven late rainy season forecast. The crisis is driven by the same IOD/Super El Niño dry-season intensification suppressing rainfall across the Maritime Continent.

items.headline: Europe Wildfires UPDATED September 16/17: 668,035 ha Burned Per EFFIS — Up from 660,528 ha; Nearly Double 20-Year Average of 346,567 ha; Worst Season Since 2017; Iberian Peninsula and Western Balkans Fire Danger Continues
items.summary: EFFIS updated the 2026 European wildfire total to 668,035 hectares as of September 16–17, up from the 660,528 hectares reported on September 9. The 2026 total is nearly double the 20-year average (2006–2025) of 346,567 hectares for this date and represents the worst wildfire season in Europe since 2017. Extreme fire danger continues in the Iberian Peninsula, Pyrenees, and western Balkans. The season is driven by western Europe's hottest summer on record (2.54°C above the 1991–2020 average) and drought conditions accumulating from early spring. The total is expected to continue growing as autumn fire weather persists in southern Europe.

items.source: Pakistan NDMA / The Express Tribune / Gulf News
items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Flood Alert: Monsoon Death Toll 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured; GB, KPK, Punjab, Balochistan Flash Flood Risk; Urban Flooding Lahore, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi; Final Monsoon Active Phase Through Late September
items.summary: Pakistan's NDMA flood alert covers Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan with heavy monsoon rainfall warnings. The nationwide monsoon death toll stands at 234 dead and 596 injured since late June — up from 183 dead/515 injured as of September 11. Flash flood risks cover GB's Gilgit, Diamer, Ghizer, Nagar, Hunza, Skardu, and Shigar districts, and KPK's Upper Dir, Swat, Bajaur, Malakand, and Kohistan. Urban flooding continues across Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi. Ongoing monitoring continues as the final monsoon active phase extends through late September.

renewables.overview_html: No major new deal announcements in the September 18 window; the prior-week transactions remain the primary story. EnerSynk + ZESCO’s 500 MW/25-year Zambia Copperbelt PPA (September 16) — the country’s largest-ever renewable contract, replacing drought-hit Zambezi hydropower in the copper-mining supply chain — remains the standout sub-Saharan transaction. Earlier deals carry forward: UK DCO approval for Morecambe + Morgan offshore wind transmission (September 15); Econergy’s €134.3 million acquisition of Escofi’s 740 MW French wind platform (September 15); Masdar + Luxcara’s €5 billion+ Germany offshore wind + BESS MoU (September 14); Gennaker 976.5 MW Baltic Sea financial close at €3 billion+ (September 11); Enel’s $760 million U.S. solar acquisition from Excelsior Energy Capital (September 11); and India’s 16.39 GW renewable additions in April–July 2026, tracking ~50 GW annually.

items.headline: Zambia Inks 25-Year PPA for 500 MW Solar Project — EnerSynk + ZESCO Copperbelt; Zambia’s Largest-Ever Renewable Contract; First Large-Scale Solar Targeting Copper Industry Power Supply Chain; Replaces Drought-Hit Zambezi Hydropower
items.summary: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd signed a 25-year power purchase agreement on September 16 for a 500 MW solar PV project in Zambia's Copperbelt province — the country's largest-ever renewable energy contract. The project is the first large-scale solar investment specifically targeting the copper-mining industry's power supply chain, which accounts for approximately 70% of Zambia's total power demand. The plant reduces ZESCO's dependence on hydropower that has suffered repeated curtailments in 2026 under drought driven by the positive IOD and Super El Niño teleconnection, directly disrupting copper-smelting operations. EnerSynk will develop, finance, own, and operate the facility under the 25-year PPA.

items.headline: UK Secretary of State Approves DCO for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan Offshore Wind Transmission Assets — Full Consent Package Complete; Export Cables, Substations + Grid to Penwortham; >500,000 UK Households
items.summary: UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets serving both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 15. The consent covers offshore export cables, landfall infrastructure, onshore cables, substations, and grid connection to the National Grid substation at Penwortham, Lancashire, completing the full regulatory package for Morecambe — which received its generation DCO in December 2025. The joint transmission DCO also covers the separately re-tendered Morgan project, which will share infrastructure. The 35-turbine project will power over 500,000 UK households.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / reNEWS / Yahoo Finance
items.headline: Econergy Acquires Escofi — 740 MW French Onshore Wind Platform for €134.3 Million: 128 MW Operational, 34 MW Under Construction, 578 MW in Development; >90% Operating Capacity Under 20-Year French CfDs at >€80/MWh; Econergy’s Entry into France
items.summary: Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi, a private French onshore wind developer and operator founded in 1988, for €134.3 million on September 15 — Econergy's entry into France. Escofi's 740 MW portfolio comprises 128 MW in commercial operation, 34 MW under construction (operations by 2027), 147 MW in advanced development with building permits secured, and 432 MW in early-to-mid development. More than 90% of operational and under-construction capacity benefits from 20-year Contracts for Difference under France's CfD regime at above €80/MWh. The acquisition expands Econergy's European wind portfolio alongside existing assets in Poland, Romania, and the UK.

items.source: offshoreWIND.biz / Energy Storage News / Energy Global
items.headline: Masdar + Luxcara Sign €5 Billion+ MoU for Germany Battery Storage and Offshore Wind — Signed During UAE State Visit to Berlin; Potential Expansion to Other European Markets
items.summary: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) and Luxcara signed an MoU on September 14 to explore joint investment in excess of €5 billion in battery energy storage systems and offshore wind projects in Germany, announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin. The partnership targets co-development, financing, and ownership of large-scale BESS and offshore wind infrastructure with possible expansion to other European markets. Masdar brings sovereign-backed scale and an existing German pipeline; Luxcara contributes domestic market expertise and established grid-connection relationships. Germany's 2026 offshore wind tenders require co-located BESS, driving this market. The MoU is subject to definitive agreements and customary regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Skyborn Renewables + Stadtwerke München Close €3 Billion+ Financing for 976.5 MW Gennaker Offshore Wind (German Baltic Sea) — Amazon 600 MW PPA; Uniper 100 MW PPA; SWM 25% Equity; Target Commercial Operations End-2028
items.summary: Skyborn Renewables and Stadtwerke München reached financial close on September 11 for the 976.5 MW Gennaker offshore wind farm in the German Baltic Sea. The financing totals €2.1 billion non-recourse project finance from 16 commercial lenders and the EIB, mobilising more than €3 billion total investment. Long-term PPAs include 600 MW to Amazon and 100 MW to Uniper. SWM holds a 25% equity stake. The 63-turbine Siemens Gamesa project will generate approximately 3.8 TWh annually, targeting commercial operations end-2028.

items.headline: Enel Green Power Acquires Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah) + Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Tennessee) From Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million — PacifiCorp 20-Year PPA; Meta Energy Off-take; TVA Contract
items.summary: Excelsior Energy Capital completed the $760 million sale of the Faraday Solar Plant (682 MW DC / 525 MW AC, Utah County, Utah — 20-year PacifiCorp PPA with Meta purchasing energy attributes) and Skyhawk Solar Plant (~128 MW DC, Obion County, Tennessee — TVA long-term PPA) to Enel Green Power North America on September 11. Combined ~810 MW DC / 625 MW AC of contracted U.S. solar capacity, expanding Enel Green Power's footprint in PJM and TVA service territories.

items.headline: India Renewable Additions: 16.39 GW in April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); BESS Growing Faster Than Generation; On Track for ~50 GW Annual FY2026–27
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the first four months of FY2026–27 (April–July 2026): 14.33 GW solar PV and 2.04 GW wind. Battery energy storage system additions are growing on a percentage basis faster than either solar or wind, reflecting MNRE's push to pair storage with intermittent generation. The April–July run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual additions in FY2026–27 — which would be a record and sustain India's position as the third-largest global renewable market.

science.overview_html: The headline peer-reviewed result for September 18 is a landmark attribution finding: Foster & Rahmstorf, “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly,” GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17 (September 16), achieves the first statistically confirmed acceleration of the forced warming trend since ~2015 at >98% confidence across five temperature datasets (NASA, NOAA, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) after removing ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability — the underlying trend is now warming faster than any prior decade in the 177-year record. In ML/AI weather modelling, new contributions include: arXiv:2609.08412 — Stochastically Perturbed Weights, a zero-marginal-cost method for generating calibrated ensembles from any deterministic ML weather model (Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, AIFS) by perturbing weight tensors at inference time, achieving CRPSS 0.04–0.13 below trained-probabilistic baselines at 10-day lead with no retraining required; and from the prior window, arXiv:2609.12815 BEAST — 700M-parameter Bayesian Swin Transformer trained on JUPITER’s 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs generating 96-member weight-space ensembles competitive with ECMWF AIFS on extreme weather metrics (September 11). The stratospheric chemistry finding from van Herpen et al. Nature Communications (September 15) — Hunga Tonga aerosol layer catalysed CH4 oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day via Cl-radical pathway absent from CMIP7 models — and the Nature Geoscience 300-year jet stream analysis (September 10): Atlantic–European jet strengthened 0.13 SD since pre-industrial while producing fewer extreme excursions remain the other window highlights.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Faster Than Any Prior Decade in 177-Year Record After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.meta: Foster & Rahmstorf · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Vol. 53, Issue 17 · doi:10.1029/2025GL118804 · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply a natural-variability filtering methodology across five major global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5 reanalysis) to isolate the forced long-term warming signal from ENSO variability (via ONI), major volcanic eruptions, and the 11-year solar cycle. The residual warming signal shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year instrumental record. Prior studies had suggested acceleration but could not rule out natural variability as the source; this study closes that attribution gap. The implied non-linearity in the forced warming trend is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The timing since approximately 2015 coincides with the onset of the sustained period of anomalous global sea surface temperatures and the string of record-warm years from 2023 onward. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active in this digest window.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.08412 — Stochastically Perturbed Weights (SPW): Zero-Marginal-Cost Calibrated Ensembles From Deterministic ML Weather Models (Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, AIFS); CRPSS 0.04–0.13 Below Trained-Probabilistic Baselines at 10-Day Lead; Architecture-Specific Injection
items.meta: Adamov et al. · arXiv:2609.08412 · Submitted to Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems (AMS) · September 2026
items.summary: Adamov et al. propose Stochastically Perturbed Weights (SPW), a method for generating calibrated probabilistic ensembles from any deterministic machine-learning weather model by perturbing the network's raw weight tensors at inference time — requiring zero additional training computation. A three-phase ablation tests SPW across four deterministic backbones (Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, AIFS), benchmarked against trained-probabilistic models (AIFS-ENS, FourCastNet 3, Atlas, IFS-ENS operational ECMWF ensemble). At 240-hour lead times, SPW ensembles achieve Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Scores 0.04–0.13 below the best trained-probabilistic baseline while requiring no marginal training cost. The key limitation: the productive injection site is architecture-specific, making SPW a per-model tuning procedure rather than a universal plug-and-play recipe. The result is practically significant for organisations already deploying deterministic models operationally that want calibrated uncertainty estimates without the cost of training separate ensemble members.

items.source: arXiv / Jülich Supercomputing Centre / JUPITER / Helmholtz AI
items.headline: arXiv 2609.12815 (BEAST): Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer on JUPITER (20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs, 3.96 EFLOP/s); 700M Parameters; 96-Member Weight-Space Ensemble; Competitive With ECMWF AIFS on Extreme Weather Metrics
items.summary: BEAST (Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer) is trained on the JUPITER supercomputer — the first exaflop-class European HPC system — using 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips at 3.96 EFLOP/s. The 700-million-parameter model generates 96 ensemble members via weight-space sampling, producing calibrated probabilistic outputs without the overhead of explicit multi-model ensembles. On benchmark evaluations for extreme weather events, BEAST achieves skill competitive with ECMWF's AIFS and operational NWP ensemble systems. The Bayesian ensemble approach directly addresses the central limitation of deterministic AI weather models: underrepresentation of forecast uncertainty for low-probability high-impact events — relevant to the Pakistan monsoon flooding, European flash floods, and Typhoon Dujuan development tracked in this digest window.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed Anomalous CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From CMIP7 Models; Potential Net Cooling Offset in Large-Eruption/Injection Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai volcanic eruption's extraordinary stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane-oxidation pathway involving chlorine radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS limb-emission satellite observations, the authors quantify the CH₄ oxidation rate at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km altitude during the peak aerosol period, sufficient to explain the anomalous formaldehyde column of approximately 12 ppb observed at 30 km — roughly 8× the background stratospheric HCHO abundance. The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models. The authors note that if large volcanic eruptions or proposed sulphate aerosol injection interventions produce aerosol layers of comparable optical depth, this CH₄ oxidation pathway could constitute a net cooling offset not currently captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience: “A Strengthening Yet Less Extreme Atlantic–European Jet During Winter” — 300-Year Record (1725–2100); Jet Strengthened 0.13 SD Since Pre-Industrial; Projected to Continue Strengthening But With Fewer Extreme Excursions; Implications for European Windstorms and Blocking
items.meta: Brönnimann, Brugnara & Kallabis · Nature Geoscience (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02069-z · Published 10 September 2026
items.summary: Brönnimann, Brugnara, and Kallabis present a 300-year analysis of daily Atlantic–European jet stream variability using four long European pressure station records combined with climate model ensemble projections. Since the pre-industrial period the jet has strengthened by 0.13 standard deviations and shifted poleward. Future projections show continued strengthening through 2100, but with extremes in jet speed, latitude, and tilt becoming less frequent — the counterintuitive result that a stronger jet has reduced variance in its most anomalous states. Key implication: the most destructive European windstorms and the most persistent blocking-driven heat waves (of the type that defined western Europe's record summer 2026) may become less frequent even as mean circulation intensifies, though uncertainties in blocking-regime projections remain large.

items.source: arXiv / Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research / University of Bergen
items.headline: arXiv 2609.11696: WRF Dynamical vs Diffusion-Model Generative Downscaling for Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation at 3-Week Lead Times — WRF Wins Non-Stationary Multicell Events; Diffusion More Consistent on Stationary Supercells; Both Beat Raw ECMWF
items.summary: Head-to-head evaluation of WRF dynamical downscaling versus a diffusion-based deep generative model, downscaling ECMWF subseasonal forecasts for two physically distinct extreme precipitation events at lead times up to 3 weeks. Both approaches substantially improve on raw ECMWF outputs. WRF achieves highest probabilistic skill for a multicell non-stationary event where the dynamical core's explicit physics captures large-scale forcing. The diffusion model outperforms WRF on a stationary supercell event and is more consistent across metrics overall, suggesting regime-adaptive or ensemble downscaling frameworks for operational S2S extreme precipitation prediction rather than a single fixed approach.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions to Be Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing that only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently covered by insurance — a structural gap that leaves households, farmers, and municipalities absorbing the remainder and creates sovereign fiscal risk during compound extreme-weather years. The Alliance will bring together insurers, investors, risk modellers, regulators, and policyholders to develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric insurance instruments — paying on measurable thresholds such as rainfall levels or temperatures rather than assessed losses — for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 668,035 ha per EFFIS September 17 with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion in Germany, France, Spain, and the Alpine states alone. Critics said the Alliance would not close the protection gap without stronger action including mandatory natural-hazard cover; the scheme aims to relieve national budgets from acting as the “insurer of last resort” during catastrophe years.

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product is a grid monitoring device that harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating the need for external power supplies, batteries, or fibre-optic ground wires. The device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data to grid operators; the self-powered design makes it viable for remote high-voltage corridors where conventional monitoring costs are prohibitive, directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and the NATO dual-use energy security priority driving NIF’s participation.

items.title: Premier Energies + RCT India Form 12 GWh BESS Manufacturing Joint Venture in Telangana — India’s Largest Planned Battery Storage Manufacturing Partnership; Phase 1: 6 GWh by June 2027; Export-Oriented from Phase 2
items.body_html: Premier Energies, the Hyderabad-based publicly listed solar cell and module manufacturer, and RCT India, a battery energy storage system developer, announced a joint venture on September 11 to manufacture 12 GWh of BESS annually at a new Telangana facility, Phase 1 targeting 6 GWh by June 2027. The JV positions Premier Energies to extend supply-chain integration from solar PV manufacturing into the adjacent BESS market, at a moment when India’s BESS additions are growing faster on a percentage basis than either solar or wind — reflecting MNRE’s push to pair storage mandatorily with large-scale renewable plants. The 12 GWh annual manufacturing target would be one of the largest domestically manufactured BESS pipelines in India, serving accelerating state-level procurement tenders across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Telangana; the JV is export-oriented from Phase 2.
